precepts.text: Destroy all the places where the nations served their gods, under every green tree.
precepts.point: Groves of trees are where the nations worshipped, and powerful men still gather at such places.

note.label: Christmas/ Icons, Idolatry, White Supremacy !!revealed!!

precepts.why:
Our commandment from our God was to destroy their altars, break their images and cut down their groves. A grove is trees, and they were cut down because they were sacred trees. Moses gives the same command in Deuteronomy: “Ye shall utterly destroy all the places, wherein the nations which ye shall possess served their gods”. Destroy the places where the nations served their gods, wherever they are.

Watch where those places were: “upon the high mountains, and upon the hills, and under every green tree”. Not some trees. Under every green tree: evergreen, oak, cedar, palm, pine. Any place they served gods on a high mountain or a high hill, destroy it, and every place under a green tree, destroy it.

Read verse 3 and the command goes further: “And ye shall overthrow their altars, and break their pillars, and burn their groves with fire”. Burn the groves with fire. The Bohemian Grove, where most of the presidents, if not all of them, have gone, has an idol of Molech, the owl, standing under trees so tall all you see is the stalk. Don't focus on the owl; look at what surrounds it. The idol is under the tree. If we were in power today, that owl would be destroyed and those trees burned all around it. Burn it all.

That is why the tree matters for Exodus 34:13. The groves Israel was told to cut down are the trees the heathen worship under, and the tree set up in the house at Christmas is the same thing.

precepts.text: What thing soever I command you, observe to do it; observing to do it is obligated, not optional, and thou shalt not add thereto nor diminish from it.
precepts.point: The watered down versions such as the NIV and ESV show what taking away looks like: many of them remove Matthew 18:11 and other scriptures, and they have taken out the Apocrypha.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
Moses says it again: “What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it.” Observing to do it is obligated, not optional, and the charge is the same as here: “Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it”.

This was spoken around 1500 BC, and on the last page of the Bible the same charge closes the book. The prophets across millenniums and captivities all speak the same thing, Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Christ and John, and that consistency proves the Bible is a true book, because twenty people cannot keep one story straight for five minutes.

precepts.text: He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel; he hath not dealt so with any nation. Keep this precept under your belt, it is brought out almost every camp.
precepts.point: The whole book of Deuteronomy is the Lord speaking unto his people Israel; he showed his statutes and his judgments to no other nation.

note.label: Deuteronomy 12: The Place Where the Lord Puts His Name

precepts.why:
“He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them. Praise ye the Lord.” The statutes and judgments Moses sets out here, “which ye shall observe to do in the land”, were shown to Jacob and to Israel, and to no other nation. The whole book of Deuteronomy is the Lord speaking unto his people Israel.

The land itself was given to the fathers while other nations were living in it, and Israel went to war with those nations to take it; the statutes and judgments belong to Israel in that land, “all the days that ye live upon the earth.” The other nations have not known his judgments; he has not dealt so with any of them. Keep Psalms 147:19-20 under your belt: it is brought out almost every camp.

precepts.text: Israel secretly built high places, set up images and groves under every green tree, and served idols, whereof the Lord had said, ye shall not do this thing.
precepts.point: Because Israel served the gods of the nations, the Most High gave those nations the rule over Israel; that is how they became the oppressor, and the word says envy not the oppressor and choose none of his ways. Unlearned and lost brothers and sisters today are still serving other gods, whatever the religion calls itself.

note.label: Deuteronomy 12: The Place Where the Lord Puts His Name

precepts.why:
Israel was told to utterly destroy all the places where the nations served their gods, “upon the high mountains, and upon the hills, and under every green tree”. Even after being warned, Israel was still idolatrous. “And the children of Israel did secretly those things that were not right against the Lord their God, and they built them high places in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city. And they set them up images and groves in every high hill, and under every green tree”.

The very places they were commanded to destroy, they built. “And there they burnt incense in all the high places, as did the heathen whom the Lord carried away before them; and wrought wicked things to provoke the Lord to anger: For they served idols, whereof the Lord had said unto them, Ye shall not do this thing.” The Lord carried the heathen away before Israel for those very works, and Israel did them secretly in every city.

Because Israel served the gods of the nations, the Most High gave those nations the rule over Israel. That is how they became the oppressor. And unlearned and lost brothers and sisters today are still serving other gods, whatever the religion calls itself.

precepts.text: Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.
precepts.point: Because Israel served the gods of the nations, the Most High gave those nations the rule over Israel; that is how they became the oppressor, and the word says envy not the oppressor and choose none of his ways. Unlearned and lost brothers and sisters today are still serving other gods, whatever the religion calls itself.

note.label: Deuteronomy 12: The Place Where the Lord Puts His Name

precepts.why:
“Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” The nations became the oppressor because Israel served their gods: the Most High gave those nations the rule over Israel. So the word says do not envy them and do not choose their ways, the very ways Israel was told to destroy upon the high mountains, upon the hills, and under every green tree.

Israel chose those ways, built high places and groves under every green tree as the heathen did, and that is what put Israel under the oppressor. Unlearned and lost brothers and sisters today are still choosing his ways, still serving other gods, whatever the religion calls itself. Choose none of his ways.

precepts.text: I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name might be there, and have chosen David to be over my people.
precepts.point: Unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose out of all your tribes to put his name there shall ye seek: out of all the tribes he chose Jerusalem as the place for his name and the temple.

note.label: Deuteronomy 12: The Place Where the Lord Puts His Name

precepts.why:
“But I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name might be there; and have chosen David to be over my people Israel.” Moses said the Lord would choose a place “out of all your tribes to put his name there”, and here is the choice: out of all the tribes he chose Jerusalem as the place for his name and the temple, and he chose David to be over his people Israel.

That is the habitation Israel was to seek and come to: “even unto his habitation shall ye seek, and thither thou shalt come”. The place was not left for Israel to pick; the Lord chose it, and the place where he put his name is Jerusalem.

precepts.text: Arise ye, and depart, for this is not your rest; it is polluted, it shall destroy you with a sore destruction.
precepts.point: Arise ye and depart does not mean to leave physically; it means come up out of the ways of this place, because it is polluted. Israel waits for the time when the third part has repented, the hundred forty and four thousand are sealed, and Christ returns to take his people out of this place and set them back in their own land.

note.label: Deuteronomy 12: The Place Where the Lord Puts His Name

precepts.why:
“Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest: because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction.” Moses told Israel “ye are not as yet come to the rest and to the inheritance”: the rest is when the Lord gives “rest from all your enemies round about, so that ye dwell in safety”. Micah says the same of where Israel is now, and this is why the scripture is pulled out on the street: this is not our rest. Israel today dwells among its enemies and serves them for food, shelter, and clothing, as Deuteronomy 28 declares. That is not rest from all your enemies round about.

Arise ye and depart does not mean to leave physically. It means come up out of the ways of this place, because it is polluted, and it shall destroy you with a sore destruction. Israel waits for the time when the third part has repented, the hundred forty and four thousand are sealed, and Christ returns to take his people out of this place and set them back in their own land. Then comes the rest and the inheritance which the Lord giveth.

precepts.text: The unclean and the clean person shall eat it alike, as the roebuck and as the hart; the unclean and clean here are persons.
precepts.point: The unclean and the clean that may eat thereof are unclean and clean persons, not unclean meats; Israel had servants then and will have servants again.

note.label: Deuteronomy 12: The Place Where the Lord Puts His Name

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt eat it within thy gates: the unclean and the clean person shall eat it alike, as the roebuck, and as the hart.” Here the same words are spelled out: the unclean and the clean are persons. So when Deuteronomy 12:15 says “the unclean and the clean may eat thereof, as of the roebuck, and as of the hart”, the unclean and the clean that may eat are unclean and clean persons, not unclean meats.

Israel had servants then and will have servants again; clean and unclean persons alike could eat the flesh killed in the gates, as the roebuck and as the hart. The verse is not opening the door to unclean meat; it is saying who may eat.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing; the lusting of the soul sits inside the dietary law.
precepts.point: The unclean and the clean that may eat thereof are unclean and clean persons, not unclean meats; Israel had servants then and will have servants again.

note.label: Deuteronomy 12: The Place Where the Lord Puts His Name

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing.” “whatsoever thy soul lusteth after” is not license to eat anything. The lusting of the soul sits inside the dietary law: it stays within the guidelines of the clean foods, “as of the roebuck, and as of the hart”, the beasts listed in chapter 14. Whatever the soul lusts after has to be one of those, because the law says thou shalt not eat any abominable thing.

So the freedom to kill and eat flesh in all thy gates, “according to the blessing of the Lord thy God which he hath given thee”, is freedom within the clean foods, never outside them.

precepts.text: They did not destroy the nations, but were mingled among the heathen, served their idols which were a snare unto them, and sacrificed their sons and daughters unto devils, and the wrath of the Lord was kindled against his people.
precepts.point: The wrath of the Lord was kindled insomuch that he abhorred his own inheritance; that snare is why Israel is where it is now, scattered among the heathen and serving them.

note.label: Deuteronomy 12: The Place Where the Lord Puts His Name

precepts.why:
Moses warned Israel not to be snared by inquiring after the gods of the nations, saying, “How did these nations serve their gods? even so will I do likewise.” Israel has a history of following what the other nations do, and the psalm records the snare fulfilled: “They did not destroy the nations, concerning whom the Lord commanded them: But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works. And they served their idols: which were a snare unto them.”

They did exactly what Moses said not to do. Instead of destroying the nations, they mingled with them, learned how those nations served their gods, and served them likewise. It went as far as the very abomination the Lord warned of here: “Yea, they sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils, And shed innocent blood, even the blood of their sons and of their daughters, whom they sacrificed unto the idols of Canaan: and the land was polluted with blood.”

“Thus were they defiled with their own works, and went a whoring with their own inventions. Therefore was the wrath of the Lord kindled against his people, insomuch that he abhorred his own inheritance.” That snare is why Israel is where it is now, scattered among the heathen and serving them. The Lord abhorred his own inheritance because his people inquired after the gods of the nations and did likewise.

precepts.text: Whatsoever thy soul lusteth after, as of the roebuck and as of the hart: the lusting of the soul is bounded by the clean beasts of this chapter.
precepts.point: The chapter then lists the clean beasts, the beasts that part the hoof and chew the cud, the fish with fins and scales, and the clean fowls; the rest of chapter 14 is clear cut on the laws of the clean and the unclean foods.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing” rules the whole chapter. Chapter 12 said “thou mayest kill and eat flesh in all thy gates, whatsoever thy soul lusteth after, according to the blessing of the Lord thy God which he hath given thee: the unclean and the clean may eat thereof, as of the roebuck, and as of the hart.”

That whatsoever thy soul lusteth after sits inside the guidelines of clean foods: as of the roebuck, as of the hart, clean beasts. The lusting of the soul is bounded by the clean beasts of this chapter; you cannot eat anything you want.

Some of our people, still unlearned, think that as long as they pray over it they can eat it. That is not true; it is a misunderstanding carried out of the New Testament. The law says thou shalt not eat any abominable thing, and the chapter then lists the clean beasts, the beasts that part the hoof and chew the cud, the fish with fins and scales, and the clean fowls. The rest of chapter 14 is clear cut on the laws of the clean and the unclean foods.

precepts.text: Take heed that thou be not snared by following them, and that thou enquire not after their gods, saying, How did these nations serve their gods?
precepts.point: Because Israel disobeyed, the sentence falls: I will not drive them out from before you, but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you. The people lifted up their voice and wept, called the place Bochim, and sacrificed there unto the Most High.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why:
Why should the inhabitants not dwell in the land? Because dwelling among them breeds curiosity after their gods. “Take heed to thyself that thou be not snared by following them, after that they be destroyed from before thee; and that thou enquire not after their gods, saying, How did these nations serve their gods? even so will I do likewise.” How did these nations serve their gods? What is that thing they are doing with that tree, what are they hanging on the tree, why are they giving each other gifts? That curiosity is the snare.

“Thou shalt not do so unto the Lord thy God: for every abomination to the Lord, which he hateth, have they done unto their gods; for even their sons and their daughters they have burnt in the fire to their gods.” The Most High said, “Observe and hear all these words which I command thee, that it may go well with thee, and with thy children after thee for ever”. Israel did not, and the angel at Bochim told them their gods shall be a snare unto you.

precepts.text: What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it.
precepts.point: Because Israel disobeyed, the sentence falls: I will not drive them out from before you, but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you. The people lifted up their voice and wept, called the place Bochim, and sacrificed there unto the Most High.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why: “What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it.” Enquiring after the nations’ gods, how did they serve them, even so will I do likewise, is adding to the Most High’s commandments. He said make no league with the inhabitants of the land and throw down their altars; we are not to add to that or take away from it. Israel had not observed to do it, and so at Bochim they lifted up their voice and wept.

precepts.text: What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it; the Most High made a law for the bright ideas that come along the way of following instructions, and it is plain.
precepts.point: Saul deflects again, the same blame game as chapter 13: They have brought them from the Amalekites, for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen, to sacrifice unto the Lord thy God; and the rest we have utterly destroyed. Verse 9 already told us Saul and the people spared them; now suddenly it is only the people, and for a good reason, a sacrifice, as though the Lord ought to be pleased.

note.label: 1 Samuel 15: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice

precepts.why:
Samuel rose early to meet Saul, and it was told him that Saul “came to Carmel, and, behold, he set him up a place”, a monument to himself. When your transgression becomes the lesson, be thankful when the correction comes quietly and nobody knows your name. Do not take the spirit of bitterness, because you deserved a lot more.

The first thing out of Saul’s mouth is a fabrication, knowing full well he transgressed: “Blessed be thou of the Lord: I have performed the commandment of the Lord.” Samuel answers, “What meaneth then this bleating of the sheep in mine ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear?” If you performed the commandment, why do I hear animals?

Saul deflects again, the same blame game as chapter 13: “They have brought them from the Amalekites: for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen, to sacrifice unto the Lord thy God; and the rest we have utterly destroyed.” Verse 9 already told us Saul and the people spared them; now suddenly it is only the people, and for a good reason, a sacrifice, as though the Lord ought to be pleased.

“What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it.” The Most High made a law for the bright ideas that come along the way of following instructions, and it is plain.

precepts.text: The nations' places of worship on the mountains, hills, and under every green tree were to be utterly destroyed, not imitated.
precepts.point: He sacrifices and burns incense in the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree, the very idolatry the law forbade.

note.label: 2 Kings 16: Ahaz and the Altar of Damascus

precepts.why:
“Ye shall utterly destroy all the places, wherein the nations which ye shall possess served their gods, upon the high mountains, and upon the hills, and under every green tree.” Their altars overthrown, their pillars broken, their groves burned, their graven images hewn down. “Ye shall not do so unto the Lord your God.”

Ahaz did the very thing the law forbade. He “sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places, and on the hills, and under every green tree.” He made his son to pass through the fire “according to the abominations of the heathen, whom the Lord cast out from before the children of Israel.”

The nations’ places of worship were to be utterly destroyed, not imitated. Ahaz walked in the way of the kings of Israel and imitated them.

precepts.text: The law had already commanded Israel to destroy such high places, not build them.
precepts.point: They wrought wicked things to provoke the Most High and served idols, though He had said plainly, ye shall not do this thing.

note.label: 2 Kings 17: The Carrying Away of Israel

precepts.why:
“Ye shall utterly destroy all the places, wherein the nations which ye shall possess served their gods, upon the high mountains, and upon the hills, and under every green tree.” Overthrow their altars, break their pillars, burn their groves, hew down their graven images.

The law had already commanded Israel to destroy such high places, not build them. Instead Israel “built them high places in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city. And they set them up images and groves in every high hill, and under every green tree.” They walked in the statutes of the heathen and served idols, “whereof the Lord had said unto them, Ye shall not do this thing.” That is why the captivity came.

precepts.text: Take heed you be not snared to inquire after the heathen's gods; add not to nor diminish from His commandments.
precepts.point: They served idols, sacrificed their sons and daughters to devils, and shed innocent blood, polluting the land and going a-whoring with their own inventions.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

precepts.why:
“They did not destroy the nations, concerning whom the Lord commanded them: But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works.” The command had warned of exactly this: “Take heed to thyself that thou be not snared by following them, after that they be destroyed from before thee; and that thou enquire not after their gods, saying, How did these nations serve their gods? even so will I do likewise.”

“Thou shalt not do so unto the Lord thy God: for every abomination to the Lord, which he hateth, have they done unto their gods; for even their sons and their daughters they have burnt in the fire to their gods.” That is what Israel learned from the heathen: they sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils and shed innocent blood, and the land was polluted with blood.

“What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it.” Add not to his commandments nor diminish from them. Israel's own inventions, the works they learned from the nations they should have destroyed, were the snare.

precepts.point: Only through Christ could all 12 tribes receive salvation.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
The law fixed the sacrifice to one place: “unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose out of all your tribes to put his name there, even unto his habitation shall ye seek, and thither thou shalt come: And thither ye shall bring your burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, and your tithes, and heave offerings of your hand, and your vows, and your freewill offerings, and the firstlings of your herds and of your flocks.”

That place was Jerusalem. When Jeroboam forbade the northern kingdom to go up there, they were cut off from the only place the sacrifices could be brought. Under the old covenant of circumcision and animal sacrifice they had no way to be saved; that is why the doctrine of the false brethren could not stand.
